findings.failure_path: Submit a pure owner Markdown deletion and a source-refuted row whose backticked zero-loss pointer is `../../some-readable-file#common-text`, or points to an in-repository symlink escaping the checkout. File.join does not reject traversal, File.file? and File.read follow the resolved target, and body.include? accepts the matching substring. zero_loss_ok and source_refuted therefore become true using content outside the frozen repository, lifting the owner RED floor; a large target can also force an unbounded whole-file read.
findings.smallest_fix: Require a repository-relative tracked regular-file path: reject absolute and `..` components, resolve symlinks, verify the real path remains beneath root and has the expected tree mode at row_scope.head, then add traversal, escaping-symlink, and oversized-target regression cases.

findings.failure_path: Acceptance case F promises unchanged behavior for RED-baseline, semantic-control, wording-only, and identifier-rename, but the test creates only one valid RED-baseline row. The supplied diff contains no executable positive or negative cases for the other three classes, so regressions in their parsing, observed-failure constraints, or owner-floor interaction can ship while all eleven new cases remain green.
findings.smallest_fix: Expand case F, or add focused cases, covering valid and critical invalid paths for semantic-control and both not-required classes, including their interaction with the new owner-floor logic.

concern_results.conclusion: The pure-deletion classifier is structurally strict, but source-refuted can still pass using a zero-loss pointer outside the repository, contrary to the evidence-map contract.
An author-controlled relative path is joined without containment checks, and symlinks are followed, allowing the shared gate to read and accept host files outside the reviewed tree.
A pure Markdown deletion plus a source-refuted row pointing through `../` or an in-repository symlink can satisfy zero_loss_ok using unrelated host content and falsely lift the RED floor.

The new tests omit path-containment and symlink cases; they also exercise only RED-baseline for acceptance case F, leaving semantic-control and both not-required compatibility claims unverified in the supplied packet.
Status parsing is additive, but the promised preservation of all existing evidence classes is not demonstrated by the supplied executable cases.
There is no migration or irreversible state change, but the shared gate is not release-ready until the evidence-pointer boundary and compatibility evidence are closed.
An out-of-tree pointer can produce a normal green result, so diagnostics provide no indication that the zero-loss evidence was outside the reviewed repository.
Containment remains bypassable because source-refuted promotes an unconstrained filesystem pointer into owner-wide evidence sufficient to waive the RED requirement.
